description: Guided C1 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Muster has the short /ʌ/ vowel in its first syllable. Master has /æ/, mister has /ɪ/, and monster has /ɑ/.
Relish begins with the short /ɛ/ vowel. Radish has /æ/, rubbish has /ʌ/, and raven has /eɪ/.
Cavern begins with /æ/. Coven begins with /ʌ/, civic with /ɪ/, and caper with /eɪ/.
Pneumatic begins with /n/ because the written p is silent. Pivotal begins with /p/, thematic with /θ/, and dramatic with /d/.
Choreography begins with /k/; ch represents /k/ in this word. Shoreline begins with /ʃ/, geography with /dʒ/, and hologram with /h/.
Gnawing begins with /n/ because the g is silent. Growing begins with /ɡr/, rowing with /r/, and showing with /ʃ/.
Corps ends with /z/ in General American. Core ends with /r/, while corpse and course end with /s/.
Lapsed ends with /pst/: the -ed ending is /t/ after the voiceless /s/. Lapse ends with /ps/, lapses with /ɪz/, and latter with /ər/.
Clenched ends with /tʃt/. Clench ends with /tʃ/, clenches with /ɪz/, and clenching with /ɪŋ/.
Accommodate is pronounced /əˈkɑmədeɪt/ and has a double c and double m. The alternatives have different vowel and consonant sequences.
Camouflage ends with /ɑʒ/ in General American. Carriage and courage end with /ɪdʒ/, while collage has a different stress and vowel pattern.
Rendezvous is pronounced /ˈrɑndəˌvuː/, with the final letters representing /vuː/. The alternatives have different syllable patterns and endings.
